summary: Source-anchored research for Ops Manager Application. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The dbi services installation guide explicitly uses a single instance for testing and proof of concept. Its standalone backing-database and HTTP examples should be read as historical lab instructions rather than a production deployment recommendation. (medium confidence)

The Ops Manager Application supplies the administrator web interface and HTTP services used by MongoDB Agents to exchange data; its web interface includes user management, host monitoring and backup management. (high confidence)
The application needs its own MongoDB database for operational information; install and start that database before starting the application. (high confidence)
mms.centralUrl identifies the application's access URL; installation walkthroughs configure it in conf/conf-mms.properties. (high confidence)

For a conventional host installation, the documented initial browser address is http://<host>:8080 and first access prompts user registration. The dbi services walkthrough demonstrates that sequence for a historical test installation. (high confidence)
The mongodb-mms script starts the application; the official init.d examples use /etc/init.d/mongodb-mms start and stop. Archive installations require the documented init.d symlink. (high confidence)

Changing the application HTTP port on a host installation requires updating mms.centralUrl in conf-mms.properties, changing BASE_PORT in mms.conf, and restarting the application. Merely changing an advertised URL does not complete the documented port-change procedure. (low confidence)

The application writes startup output under each host’s logs directory to mms#-startup.log, where # is a zero-based instance index. These logs retain startup history subject to the configured rotation policy. (low confidence)
HTTPS configuration uses a PEM file containing a valid certificate and private key. The documented HTTPS port is 8443; changing it also requires changing the access URL. (low confidence)

Creationline's 2023 evaluation of Ops Manager 6.0.13 observed roughly five minutes between systemctl reporting the service active and the web interface becoming accessible; this is one test observation, not a universal startup-time guarantee. (low confidence)

The dbi services 4.0.2 walkthrough and Creationline 6.0.13 walkthrough explicitly describe evaluation environments. Their single-instance or colocated setup examples should be read within that scope. (high confidence)

The application requires a MongoDB application database to retain operational information. MongoDB documents a dedicated replica set for this state; independent installation walkthroughs also configure a backing database before using the application. (high confidence)

Ops Manager stores global configuration in the application database. Local conf-mms.properties settings override global values, so changing a value in the Admin UI may not change effective behavior on a server with a local override. (high confidence)

Each application server needs its application-database connection and authentication configuration in conf-mms.properties. The mongo.mongoUri property identifies that connection; mms.centralUrl identifies the application access URL. (high confidence)

Bypassing the initial setup wizard requires mms.ignoreInitialUiSetup=true plus the required application configuration. The flag alone does not bypass pre-flight validation; missing required settings can prevent startup. (high confidence)

The Kubernetes Operator can deploy and maintain Ops Manager as a Kubernetes resource. Its application configuration can be supplied through spec.configuration, and externalConnectivity settings can request a service for access to the application. (high confidence)
